# SST Laravel — agent quick reference

Deploy Laravel on AWS Fargate (containers). Full docs:
`node_modules/@kirschbaum-development/sst-laravel/docs/` (guides listed in
`README.md`, every option in `api.md`).

## Setup flow (in the Laravel app folder)

```bash
npm install @kirschbaum-development/sst-laravel --save  # required: sst.config.ts imports it
npx sst-laravel skill:install            # install/update the skill (.ai/skills with Laravel Boost)
npx sst-laravel guide                    # same guide as the skill, from the installed package
npx sst-laravel doctor                   # readiness check (tools, Docker, AWS, deps, assets, env, git)
npx sst-laravel init                     # creates sst.config.ts (minimal)
composer install && npm run build        # the image copies vendor/ and public/build as they are
npx sst-laravel deploy --stage dev       # deploy (vault-aware, use instead of sst deploy); waits for the rollout, fails on rollback
npx sst-laravel status --stage dev --wait   # expected revisions + private ECR image availability + /up at the URL the deploy saved
npx sst-laravel command:run migrate:status --stage dev   # checks the database (/up does not)
npx sst-laravel logs web --stage dev --no-follow         # recent logs, no streaming
npx sst remove --stage dev               # removes stage resources; retained image manifests need separate cleanup
```

Install the package before any `npx sst-laravel` command. Until it is
installed, `npx` looks for a different, unscoped package with that name.
With several AWS profiles, `export AWS_PROFILE=<name>` before every command.
No AWS login yet: the user runs `aws configure sso` (browser), then
`aws sso login --profile <name>`; never ask for keys in the chat. Guide:
`getting-started.md#aws-access`.
Without a domain the URL is http only; https:// on the load balancer times out.

Never print secret values. Never put AWS keys in `.env` files. Never deploy to
`production` unless the user said so.

## Minimal config (web only, no domain, no database)

```ts
const app = new LaravelService("MyApp", {
  vpc,
  web: { size: "small", healthCheck: { path: "/up" } },
  config: { environment: { file: `.env.${$app.stage}` } },
});
return { url: app.url, deployment: app.deployment };
```

`new sst.aws.Vpc("MyVpc")` with no options is cheapest (~$0.50/mo). Without
NAT, containers run in public subnets with a public IP (~$3.65/mo each);
inbound traffic still only comes through the load balancer. Add `nat: "ec2"`
(~$13/mo) to keep containers private, e.g. for a fixed outbound IP. Avoid
`nat: "managed"` (~$73/mo) unless you need the scale.

Rough monthly cost of this setup in us-east-1: ~$46 (small container $18 +
its public IP $3.65, load balancer $16 + its 2 public IPs $7.30, VPC $0.50).

## Add what the user agreed to

Before any config, show the user a plan: why SST Laravel in a few bullets
(`why-sst-laravel.md`: infrastructure as code, auto-scaling, linking AWS
resources, IAM roles instead of AWS keys), what the app needs, questions
(database? background work? where the environment variables live?), what gets
created and the monthly cost, how the deploy works, and how to remove it
(`npx sst remove --stage <stage>`).

Environment options to explain: an env file on this machine (free, simplest,
only this machine can deploy), `RemoteEnvVault` in AWS Secrets Manager
(~$0.40/mo per stage, for teams and CI), plus SST secrets for a few sensitive
values and `config.environment.vars` for settings that aren't secret.

```ts
const database = new sst.aws.Postgres("MyDatabase", { vpc }); // or sst.aws.Mysql, ~$14/mo
config: { deployment: { script: "infra/deploy.sh" } },  // runs on each start: put `php artisan migrate --force` in it
link: [database],                       // auto-injects DB_*/REDIS_*/AWS_* vars
link: [{ resource: db, envFrom: (db) => ({ CUSTOM: db.host }) }], // extra vars
web: { domain: "app.example.com" },     // custom domain (https)
web: { size: "medium", scaling: { min: 1, max: 3 } },  // small|medium|large; cpu/memory win
web: { scheduler: true, tasks: { queue: { command: "php artisan queue:work" } } }, // in the web container, no extra cost
workers: [{ horizon: true, scheduler: true }],         // queues / scheduler in a worker (~$22/mo)
reverb: { domain: "ws.example.com" },   // WebSockets (or `reverb: true`)
config: { environment: { secrets: env } },  // RemoteEnvVault instead of file; env:push before deploy
link: [new sst.Secret("STRIPE_SECRET")],     // SST secret: npx sst secret set STRIPE_SECRET <value> --stage <stage>
config: { environment: { vars: { FEATURE_X: "on" } } }, // values that aren't secret (committed)
web: { advanced: { architecture: "arm64" } }, // SST escape hatch (experts only)
```

## Load balancer (web and reverb)

Secure by default, nothing to configure: TLS 1.2+ on the https listener, only
the listener ports open, invalid headers dropped, http redirected to https.

```ts
web: {
  loadBalancer: {
    ingressCidrs: ["173.245.48.0/20", "2400:cb00::/32"], // only these ranges (CDN/WAF) reach the load balancer
    accessLogs: true,                                    // access logs to a new S3 bucket, kept 90 days
    // accessLogs: { bucket, prefix: "web", retentionDays: 365 },
    // sslPolicy: "ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-Ext2-2021-06", // only to support older clients
  },
},
```

Only add these when the user asks. `ingressCidrs` blocks every other address,
so confirm the ranges first. `loadBalancer.accessLogs` is not `web.accessLogs`
(nginx logs in CloudWatch). `loadBalancer` only takes these three keys; any
other key fails the deploy. To define the load balancer itself (listeners,
ports), use `advanced.loadBalancer`. Guide: `load-balancer.md`.

## Before deploying

- `.env.<stage>` exists, `APP_KEY` set, `APP_DEBUG=false`, `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr`
  (with `RemoteEnvVault`, pushed with `env:push`).
- Stage env file is git-ignored (`git check-ignore .env.dev`).
- `bootstrap/app.php` has `$middleware->trustProxies(at: "*")`.
- Docker is running (the image builds on this machine).
- `vendor/` installed and `public/build` current; the first deploy writes a
  `.dockerignore` (git, node_modules, .env*, sqlite, uploads, logs): commit it.
- App `name` in sst.config.ts is unique in the AWS account (SST keys its
  state by app name + stage).
- No migrations at startup until a persistent database exists. Without a
  database, set `SESSION_DRIVER=cookie`, `CACHE_STORE=file`,
  `QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync` so pages still load.

## If /up is not healthy

1. `npx sst-laravel status --stage <stage> --wait` — rollout + health in one view
   (`--url <url>` for another address). "rolled back to the previous revision"
   means the new tasks failed: the app answers from the old revision.
2. `npx sst-laravel logs web --stage <stage> --no-follow` — recent errors.
3. Usual causes: missing `APP_KEY`, wrong env names, DB unreachable, wrong health
   path, AWS keys committed in the env file (use the IAM role instead).
4. `failed to configure registry cache importer ... not found` on the first
   build is expected.

## Upgrading and verification

Keep `deployment: app.deployment` in run() outputs (array for several components).
Deploy/status verify only registered services against those exact task definition
ARNs and check their private ECR images. Add external tasks explicitly via
`deployment: { ...app.deployment, taskDefinitions: [taskRunner.taskDefinition] }`;
this only checks images, not task execution, env vars, or IAM. No discovery of
unrelated services/tasks. Verification also needs ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition and
ecr:DescribeImages. --no-wait skips verification.

SST 4.17.1 / docker-build 0.0.14 work with the package Dockerfiles; no provider
pin is needed. .sst is excluded using a read-only build-context mount. Existing
pins are preserved; 0.0.22 was a verified workaround, not a proven minimum.
Only managed images default to retainOnDelete. Persist retention in a deployment
BEFORE a provider/resource replacement: adding it during replacement does not
protect the old resource. Retention cannot restore deleted images or prevent ECR
lifecycle cleanup. Retained manifests need deliberate cleanup that accounts for
active and rollback task revisions. See deploying.md#upgrading-from-071.
